content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In Christian teaching, 'year' most commonly carries the symbolic sense of a complete, divinely appointed period of time — above all 'the acceptable year of the Lord,' i.e., the era of God's favor, salvation, and release. This draws on the Jubilee year (a fiftieth-year proclamation of liberty, debt release, and restoration) as a type of messianic redemption, which Jesus applies to his own ministry in the Nazareth synagogue. Thus 'year' symbolizes the full season or epoch of God's saving activity rather than a mere calendar unit.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 61:1-2 ('to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor')","Luke 4:18-19 (Jesus reads Isaiah 61 and declares it fulfilled)","Leviticus 25:8-13 (the Year of Jubilee: liberty, release, restoration)","Isaiah 34:8 and 63:4 ('year of recompense' / 'year of my redeemed')","Genesis 1:14 (heavenly lights appointed for 'seasons, days, and years' — time ordered by God)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The year-day principle in prophetic interpretation: a symbolic 'day' in prophecy stands for a literal year, so prophetic time periods (e.g., 70 weeks = 490 years; 1260 days = 1260 years) are decoded into years. Here 'year' functions as the unit of prophetic fulfillment. This was dominant in historicist Protestant interpretation and remains central in Seventh-day Adventist and some other traditions, though it is a minority view in contemporary mainstream scholarship.","basis":["Numbers 14:34 ('each day for a year')","Ezekiel 4:5-6 ('a day for each year')","Daniel 9:24-27 (the seventy 'weeks' understood as weeks of years)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A 'year' (or the 360-day prophetic year) as the building block of apocalyptic chronology: 'a time, times, and half a time' = three and a half years, equated with 42 months and 1260 days, symbolizing a limited, God-bounded period of tribulation or persecution.","basis":["Daniel 7:25; 12:7","Revelation 11:2-3; 12:6, 14; 13:5"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Equivalence of vast divine time with human time — 'one day is as a thousand years' — used to argue that a 'year' or 'day' with God does not map onto human chronology, and in some schemes to support millennial or day-age readings.","basis":["Psalm 90:4","2 Peter 3:8"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"'Year' as simply a complete natural cycle ordained by God, marking his faithfulness in the rhythm of seasons and the liturgical/festal calendar, without a distinct symbolic freight beyond ordered time under God's sovereignty.","basis":["Genesis 1:14; 8:22","Exodus 23:14-17 (annual festal cycle)","Psalm 65:11 ('you crown the year with your bounty')"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"medium","notes":"Unlike terms such as 'lamb' or 'leaven,' 'year' does not have a single fixed symbolic meaning in Christian interpretation. The most recognizable symbolic usage is the 'year of the Lord's favor' (Jubilee/era of salvation), which is widely preached and cited, but much discussion of 'year' occurs within prophetic-chronology debates (year-day principle, prophetic 360-day year), where interpretive traditions diverge sharply (historicist vs. preterist vs. futurist vs. idealist). Any author claiming one settled symbolic meaning for 'year' is selecting from a genuinely contested field."}
